- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or overshoot after recent spikes, then sharply drop below true values.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: after a spike, forecasts remain high while true values decline toward historical mean.
- Forecasts lag behind true values in the middle-to-late period (days 15–25), suggesting delayed reaction to market signals.
- Model underestimates downward trends after a peak; true values often dip below forecasted lows.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values in the first 10 days, then gradually adjust — but often too late or too much.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections after a spike; tends to smooth out volatility.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) and overly pessimistic in the long term (20–30 days) — inconsistent horizon calibration.
- Model overreacts to recent high prices, leading to overestimation of future prices even when historical mean is lower.
- Forecasts often fail to account for seasonal or cyclical mean reversion patterns in EU ETS — especially in the 20–30 day window.
